clue.text: Girl's American friend making a bloomer

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A woman's American pal commits an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a gaffe, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is a flower about to open, so literally a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Cor, the shrink acts, somehow spilling ink — for this!

definitions.text: Cor, the shrink acts, somehow spilling ink — for this!

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are mixed up in some way
spilling means the letters of ink are lost from the mixture

explanation.surface: Goodness, the psychiatrist behaves oddly, splashing ink, all for a psychological test.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of COR THE SHRINK ACTS, minus INK, rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also describes the test.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rorschach test asks subjects to interpret inkblots, so a shrink spills ink for it.

clue.text: Child's play finishes with favourite bit

parts.note: a snip is something very easy, a doddle
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Child's play ends up with a favourite piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment of something.

clue.text: Impressive six maybe — one clearing loop of rope?

indicators.note: clearing means the one is taken out of the hit

parts.note: a six in cricket, hitting over the boundary, is an example of a big hit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A big six in cricket, with one ball clearing the ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six is a shot clearing the boundary rope; take I out of BIG HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: In knots a bight is a loop or slack curve in a rope.

clue.text: What could make superior young dog bend over laughing?

definitions.text: What could make superior young dog
definitions.meaning: an instruction: superior is UP, and doubling its P at both ends makes a young dog
to fold up helplessly with mirth

explanation.surface: What makes a top puppy fold up with laughter?
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic instruction rather than a dictionary definition: doubling the P in UP gives PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To double up is to bend over, as from pain or helpless laughter.

clue.text: Review showing very little's right in this county

indicators.note: the right letter is put in where the very letter stood, replacing it

parts.note: a survey is a review or general look over something
a small v is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A review shows that very little is right in this county.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the V in SURVEY for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrey is one of the English home counties, just south-west of London.

clue.text: Record-holder with something to hide?

definitions.meaning: the cardboard cover a vinyl record is stored in
a part of a garment where one hides a trick

explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is both a record cover and the arm of a garment used for concealment.

clue.text: Official is stern-but has heart right inside

indicators.note: inside means the heart and right go within the stern

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
the gist is the heart of a matter

explanation.surface: An official is stern but has his heart in the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'stern' is an adjective about the official; in the wordplay it is the back end of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official who keeps records, such as of births and marriages.

clue.text: Scientific collector of cats and dogs?

definitions.text: Scientific collector of cats and dogs?

parts.words: Scientific collector of cats and dogs?
parts.note: it raining cats and dogs is a heavy downpour, so the collector is an instrument measuring rainfall

explanation.surface: A scientist who gathers pets.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument collects precipitation, and heavy rain is idiomatically raining cats and dogs.

clue.text: Good opportunity for man to forge a partnership

parts.note: room, as in room for improvement, means scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: A fine chance for a man to set up a business partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is the man forming a marriage partnership at a wedding.

clue.text: Like a dictator involving soldiers in a great deal

indicators.note: in means the soldiers go inside the great deal

parts.note: materially means considerably, a great deal
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Acting like a tyrant, with troops involved in a large way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a dictator' reads as a simile, but the definition is an adverb of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Magisterially means in an authoritative, commanding manner, as a dictator acts.

clue.text: Get into trouble when policeman gets 'urt?

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
hurt in Cockney speech loses its H; hurt means hit, which likewise drops its H

explanation.surface: Trouble arrives when a constable gets hurt, in Cockney speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'urt signals the dropped H, so the synonym HIT also loses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is a British idiom meaning to be punished or get into trouble.

clue.text: Spending recklessly is delightful, new leader found

indicators.note: a new first letter is found for the word, replacing its leader

parts.note: ravishing means delightful or enchanting
L stands for learner, a newcomer or novice

explanation.surface: Wild spending is a delightful thing, says a new party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: RAVISHING's first letter R is replaced by L, for a learner, as on British L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavishing means giving or spending extravagantly, so spending recklessly.

clue.text: Maybe cadet performed as if on stage?

parts.note: the word cadet is one example of the letters of the first word 'out', that is, rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainee officer put on a performance, as if in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: ACTED with OUT as anagram signal gives CADET.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out is to perform or dramatise a scene, as actors do on stage.

clue.text: Tired men, struggling, need energy fix

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Exhausted men, struggling, need an energy boost.
explanation.walkthrough: TIREDMEN is rearranged to DETERMIN, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to fix or settle something definitely.

clue.text: Return of dawn — across river tree is seen

indicators.note: the turned word stretches across the river letter, holding it
return means the word for dawn is read backwards

parts.note: sunup is dawn

explanation.surface: When dawn returns, a tree is seen across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: SUNUP reversed gives PUNUS, which goes across R.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunus is the botanical genus of trees including plums, cherries and almonds.

clue.text: Companion has boarded earlier ship

indicators.note: has boarded means the companion goes onto, inside, the other word

parts.note: sooner means earlier
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A companion boarded an earlier vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, for the British honour Companion of Honour, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts.

clue.text: Cordiality shown by husband in home circle

parts.note: heart means warmth or cordiality

explanation.surface: Warmth shown by a husband within the family circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth, the fireside, stands for home and the family gathered there.

clue.text: Slander — something poisonous intrinsically

annotationWithheld.why: Slander — something poisonous intrinsically (7): ASP plus PER SE (intrinsically) telescoped, the P serving both pieces at once, which the grammar cannot express

clue.text: One at the back of the joint is a gangster

indicators.note: the one comes after the joint, at its back

parts.note: a scarf is a joint in carpentry, two timbers bevelled to overlap
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone lurking at the back of the bar is a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a dive or a body joint, but here it is a woodworking scarf joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of the American gangster Al Capone, and of a film gangster.

clue.text: Everyone to keep awfully thin? There's much work to be done here

definitions.text: There's much work to be done here

indicators.note: to keep means the everyone word holds the next piece

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of thin are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Everyone must stay terribly slim when there is so much work to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges thin into NTHI, which 'to keep' places inside the everyone word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are proverbially industrious, so their mound is a place of much work.

clue.text: Reformer's audible criticisms

indicators.note: audible means the name is heard spoken aloud

parts.note: John Knox was the Scottish Protestant reformer

explanation.surface: A reformer voices criticisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocks are adverse criticisms, as in taking knocks from the press.

clue.text: Noun operates unusually in contrived speech

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A noun works oddly in artificial language.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language, so speech that was deliberately constructed.

clue.text: African calls of disapproval before introduction of independence

indicators.note: the calls come before the next piece

parts.note: tut is a click of disapproval

indicators.note: introduction of means just the first letter of the word independence

explanation.surface: Disapproving noises greet the introduction of independence in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Small, like the numbers between twelve and twenty?

definitions.text: like the numbers between twelve and twenty?
definitions.meaning: having the quality of the teens, thirteen to nineteen

explanation.definitionFit: Teeny means tiny, and whimsically means teen-like, as numbers ending in teen are.

clue.text: Is gnawing animal going round collections of bones?

indicators.note: going round means the words Is and the animal are read backwards together

parts.note: a rat is a rodent, a gnawing animal

explanation.surface: A rodent chewing round a heap of bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' turns the whole run backwards, not just the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi, plural of tarsus, are the groups of small bones forming the ankle.

clue.text: Pleasant set entertaining six counties

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the one word holds the other

parts.note: to congeal is to set or solidify
Northern Ireland, NI, is made up of six counties

explanation.surface: A pleasant group of people hosting visitors from six counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called the Six Counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial means agreeable or pleasant, especially in company.

clue.text: Middle of area with church saints — an apse?

indicators.note: middle of means only the central letters of the word area

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: In the middle of a church area dedicated to saints sits an apse.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess in a church, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Top people's payment for literary work?

definitions.meaning: kings, queens and their families, those at the top of society
a fee paid to an author for each copy sold

explanation.definitionFit: Royalty means both the royal family and an author's per-copy fee.
